headline: Shareholder returns outpace reinvestment as pricing and buybacks intensify.

momentum_note: The Cash Harvest is accelerating across energy, materials, and financial services. ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, and CF Industries all returned more cash to shareholders than they deployed in capex during 2025-2026, with explicit public commitments to 40-50% cash-flow return targets. American Express hit its 30th straight quarter of double-digit card-fee growth, monetizing premium and captive customers. BrightSpring shows per-unit pricing momentum in pharmacy despite flat volume, a clear margin-harvesting signal. Even Charter, facing internet subscriber declines, has held connectivity revenue flat through pricing while using mobile as a growth offsetter. The only misfire is EchoStar, which is in financial distress and thus outside the pattern. The trend strengthens when commodity cycles and franchise lock-in align (energy, pharma margins, credit card fees), and leadership is openly framing capital return as a primary allocation posture rather than a residual one.
